question: Which of the following States/Union Territories is included in the 'Areas of Inadequate Rainfall' of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ladakh is a Union Territory in India that is characterized by an arid, cold desert climate due to its location in the Himalayan rain shadow region.
 
• It receives very low annual precipitation, often less than 50 mm, making it one of the areas with inadequate rainfall in India.
 
• The region's unique geography includes high-altitude plateaus and mountains, which obstruct the monsoon winds, further reducing rainfall.
 
• The scarcity of rainfall has led to the reliance on glacier meltwater for agriculture and other water needs in Ladakh.
 
• Efforts are being made to address water scarcity in Ladakh through innovative methods like artificial glaciers and community water management projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Areas of Inadequate Rainfall:**

 
 
• Regions categorized under inadequate rainfall generally receive less than 750 mm of annual rainfall.
 
• These areas include parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Ladakh, and some regions in the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Rain Shadow Effect:**
 
 
• Occurs when mountains block the passage of rain-producing weather systems, causing arid conditions on the leeward side.
 
• Ladakh is an example of a rain shadow region due to its location beyond the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Glacier Meltwater Dependency:**
 
 
• Ladakh relies heavily on meltwater from glaciers for irrigation and drinking water.
 
• Climate change is impacting glacier size and meltwater availability, posing challenges to water security.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Glacier Technology:**
 
 
• An innovative water conservation method pioneered by Sonam Wangchuk in Ladakh.
 
• Artificial glaciers store water during winter and release it during summer for agricultural use.
